name: MND medication overview
description: MND-specific overview of medicines that may slow progression and medicines used to manage symptoms such as drooling, cramping, pain, shortness of breath, constipation, anxiety and depressed mood.
care_team_notes: Frame medicine information as a discussion starter for the neurologist, GP, MND clinic, pharmacist and palliative care team; do not present treatment choices as personal medical advice.

name: Riluzole
description: Australian MND-specific information about riluzole, including purpose, expected benefit, access pathways, forms, monitoring, adverse effects and links to PBS/TGA medicine information.
care_team_notes: Use source-linked language and refer eligibility, prescribing, dose, liver monitoring, side effects and PEG/liquid questions to the treating neurologist, GP and pharmacist.

name: Edaravone / RADICAVA
description: Source-bound information on edaravone/RADICAVA, including what the treatment is, how it is administered, possible side effects and where Australian consumer medicine information may be found.
care_team_notes: Do not infer availability, suitability or funding beyond the source text; tell users to discuss access, eligibility, burden, cost and side effects with their neurologist.

name: Tofersen
description: Source-bound Australian information about tofersen for MND associated with SOD1 gene changes, including treatment boundary, provisional approval context and specialist discussion points.
care_team_notes: Only answer from retrieved sources; avoid suggesting genetic therapy unless the user has specialist-confirmed SOD1-related MND and is discussing care with a neurologist/genetics team.

name: Symptom medicines
description: High-level record for medicines used by clinicians to help symptoms such as saliva/drooling, cramps, spasticity, pain, breathlessness, constipation, reflux, sleep disturbance, anxiety and low mood.
care_team_notes: Ask about symptom severity, swallowing, breathing, PEG, current medicines and allergies; route dose/product questions to a clinician or pharmacist and cite exact source passages.

name: Medicine safety and consumer medicine information
description: Australian medicine-safety record covering consumer medicine information, product information, warnings, interactions, side effects, overdose instructions, storage and where to find official documents.
care_team_notes: For any medicine answer, encourage checking the current CMI/PI, asking a pharmacist, and keeping an up-to-date medicine list for appointments and emergency care.

name: PBS medicine access
description: PBS record for source-linked information about subsidised medicine listing, authority requirements, available brands and patient-charge context where visible in the downloaded PBS page.
care_team_notes: PBS details can change; answer with retrieval date and source link, and send eligibility or authority-prescription questions to the neurologist, GP or pharmacist.

name: Clinical trials and research treatments
description: Australian-oriented record for research treatment boundaries, clinical-trial information, trial registry searching and questions to discuss with a specialist before considering trial participation.
care_team_notes: Keep trial answers informational; never imply enrolment or suitability, and direct the user to the trial team, neurologist and official registry entry for current inclusion criteria.
